text: EBIT (Earnings Before Interest and Tax) = Gross Profit - Operating Expenses (Opex). Measures core operating profitability before financing costs and taxes.
EBITDA = EBIT + Depreciation + Amortization. Approximates operating cash flow and is widely used for comparing company performance across capital structures.
Gross Profit = Revenue - Cost of Goods Sold (COGS). Represents profit after direct production costs but before operating expenses.
Gross Margin = (Gross Profit / Revenue) * 100. Expressed as a percentage, it shows how much of each revenue dollar remains after covering COGS.
Opex (Operating Expenses) includes all costs required to run the business: headcount/salaries, marketing, IT, travel, and other overhead. Excludes COGS.
Opex Variance = ((Actual Opex - Budget Opex) / Budget Opex) * 100. A positive variance means spending exceeded budget; negative means under-spend.
Revenue (also called Net Sales or Turnover) is the total income generated from selling products or services before any expenses are deducted.
COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) includes direct costs attributable to producing the goods sold: raw materials, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead.
Net Income = EBIT - Interest Expense - Tax. The bottom-line profit after all expenses, interest, and taxes have been deducted from revenue.
ROI (Return on Investment) = ((Return - Investment) / Investment) * 100. Measures the efficiency or profitability of an investment as a percentage.
EBIT Margin = (EBIT / Revenue) * 100. Shows what percentage of revenue becomes operating profit. Higher margin indicates better operational efficiency.
Variance in finance is the difference between actual and budgeted/planned figures. Favorable variance = better than budget; Unfavorable = worse than budget.
P&L (Profit and Loss Statement) is a financial statement summarizing Revenue, COGS, Gross Profit, Opex, EBIT, and Net Income over a period.
HFM (Hyperion Financial Management) is Oracle's enterprise financial consolidation and reporting software used for multi-entity financial close and reporting.
SAP is an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. SAP FI/CO modules handle financial accounting and controlling, including P&L, cost center, and profit center reporting.
